Shortened and extended hydrocarbon chains resulted in slightly reduced (1.8-fold) binding affinities for H3 possessing K9acr (Kd = 13.7 μM) and K9pen (Kd = 13.6 μM) to the AF9 YEATS domain (Table 1, Fig. 4). The results indicate that the terminal methyl group of Kcr plays an important role in the AF9 YEATS recognition, in line with recent studies that have demonstrated a favorable Kcr-mediated desolvation and CH-π interactions. Our observation that AF9 YEATS displays high binding affinity for Kpen supports the view that the AF9 YEATS domain has an end-open aromatic pocket, ideal for interaction with prolonged and bulkier acyl chains, which also is maintained by the flexibility of the terminal group. Interestingly, AF9 YEATS displayed 1.5-fold higher binding affinity for sterically demanding H3K9cin (Kd = 5.1 μM) compared to H3K9cr, suggesting that Kcin can enhance the AF9 YEATS-H3 interaction through an additional aromatic ring. This finding suggests a potentially novel π-π-π interaction sandwiched between Phe59 and Phe28 residues of the AF9 YEATS domain and the aromatic ring of Kcin. Unlike the naturally occurring Kbz that associates with AF9 YEATS via unoptimal π-π stacking, resulting in weaker binding affinity than Kcr, longer side-chain of Kcin appears to bind via a combination of two types of π-π stacking interactions. Additionally, the binding analyses revealed that AF9 YEATS displays 6-fold and 20-fold reduced affinity for H3 possessing K9-2mecr and K9-3mecr (Kd = 46.5 μM and Kd = 159 μM), respectively, arising from the insertion of an additional methyl group at either the 2- or 3-position of the crotonyl group (Table 1). These results suggest that weaker noncovalent interactions are caused by small structural alterations in Kcr, such that the alkene of the crotonyl mark is shielded by the additional methyl group and a steric clash with AF9 YEATS might appear due to the presence of the bulkier methyl group. In addition, we observed that the AF9 YEATS domain displays a preference for H3K9cr over its trifluorinated mimic H3K9tfc, resulting in 6-fold weaker binding (Kd = 7.8 μM vs 48.5 μM) (Table 1). This result indicates that replacing the hydrogens by fluorines disrupts the energetically favorable CH-π interactions and leads to a possible repulsion with the electron-rich aromatic rings in Phe28, which can be attributed to fluorine’s high electronegativity.
